thread:
Marta: quick heads-up — after the kernel module update on prod-dedicated, 8k-token workloads show sporadic p99 spikes (~2x). perfetto trace attached. :eyes:
Ryan: can you paste the timeline screenshot or upload the trace? nsys would help too.
Marta: uploaded the perfetto link -> https://s3.company/trace/2170000011/perfetto.pb
ci-bot: Trace uploaded: s3://redwood-traces/eng-runtime/2170000011/perfetto.pb
Sam: looked at the perfetto slice — DMA stall (~10-20ms) at kernel launch + long memcpy. suspect kernel selection changed to fp16-kernel that funnels through slow memcpy path.
Ryan: interesting. did the runtime fall back to "unified-quant" path? how's KV cache behaving during those runs?
Marta: KV hitrate steady. KV cache adds small jitter, but this is separate. I'm more worried about kernel choice heuristics under long sequence lengths.
Natalie: I ran quick nsys runs on a repro box. numbers:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt,syscalls --sample=cpu --output=trace_2170000011
# full trace: wall time x12, p99 +300ms, sampling-only: overhead ~1.08x
```
Natalie: full nsys had ~12x runtime overhead and blew out SLOs. sampling (1%) gave us enough timeline to spot memcpy hotspot with negligible SLO impact.
Sam: proposal: event-driven probe that flips on when request seq_len > 4k and only for a bounded sample of requests. keep cumulative sampling <= 0.2%/hour per cluster.
Ryan: add guardrails: disable if rolling p99 > target_slo or during high CPU steal. Fallback: if probe triggers more than 5x expected, auto-scale down sampling.
Marta: config draft:
```
probe:
  trigger: seq_len>4000
  sampling_rate: 0.002   # 0.2% per request
  max_per_hour: 100
  disable_on_slo: true
  slo_window: 5m
```
Marta: also need legal + prod ops signoff for trace retention and PII scrub.
Natalie: cost eval — full traces on 10% of traffic for 1h = ~200 GPU-hours (expensive). Our safe default: sample 0.1-0.5% plus targeted canary on dedicated clusters.
Sam: implement quick server-side switch: lightweight CUPTI callback to increment probe counter and skip heavy kernel metrics unless sampled. that'll cut overhead vs full nvtx injection.
Ryan: next steps: (1) wire in on-canary with sampling_rate=0.1%, (2) run nsys sampling vs perfetto micro-trace to validate, (3) add CI check that driver bump triggers no kernel-fallback regressions.
Marta: I'll open a PR with the probe code and the config + playbook. assigning to @sam and @natalie for profiler bits. :thumbsup:
ci-bot: created issue #8993: 'event-driven probe for long sequences' -> https://gh/redwood/8993
